suggestions: Add explicit SAFE-T framework checklist to all depression/suicide MCQ explanations (Specific plan, Access to means, Feelings, Earlier attempts, Threat)

Include Aboriginal/TSI cultural safety considerations: 'Respectfully ask Aboriginal/TSI status, offer Aboriginal liaison, consider historical trauma (Stolen Generations, forced removals), use SEWB framework'

Enhance protective factors assessment in suicide risk MCQs: Link protective factors explicitly to SAFE-T risk stratification (e.g., 'Strong family support reduces but does NOT eliminate high risk if plan + means present')
Standardize medication nomenclature: Use Australian generic names exclusively (quetiapine NOT Seroquel, olanzapine NOT Zyprexa, venlafaxine NOT Effexor)
Add Mental Health Act state-specific variations to relevant MCQs (NSW 2007, VIC 2014, QLD 2016) with explicit criteria differences
Include crisis contacts in all suicide-related MCQ explanations: Lifeline 13 11 14, Beyond Blue 1300 224 636, Aboriginal/TSI crisis line 13YARN (13 92 76)
strengths: Excellent Mental Health Act compliance: MCQs correctly identify involuntary admission criteria (mentally ill, risk, refuses treatment, no alternative) - see PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-967, PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-2012, PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-2044

Strong medication safety: Correct Australian dosing (sertraline 50mg, olanzapine 5-10mg, diazepam 10mg), appropriate monitoring (lithium levels, clozapine FBC), QTc considerations - see PSY-DEP-20260125-602, PSY-PSYCHOSIS-20260125-052

Comprehensive de-escalation techniques: Verbal de-escalation emphasized before pharmacological intervention, least restrictive principle applied - aligns with Australian emergency psychiatry standards
Accurate risk stratification: High risk correctly identified (plan + means + intent + refuses help) leading to involuntary admission - see PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-2004, PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-2028
Evidence-based treatment guidelines: First-line treatments align with RANZCP/eTG (SSRIs for depression/anxiety, CBT for GAD/panic, DBT for BPD, OST for opioid use disorder)

Clear Emergency Management: Appropriate acute management for alcohol withdrawal (benzodiazepines + thiamine), stimulant psychosis (benzodiazepines + low-dose antipsychotic), NMS (stop antipsychotic, ICU, bromocriptine)
manual_review_reasons: SAFE-T framework application inconsistent across suicide-related MCQs - requires clinical expert review to ensure all depression/psychosis cases have adequate risk assessment
Cultural safety missing entirely - requires review to determine if Aboriginal/TSI considerations should be added to psychiatric MCQ explanations per Australian medical education standards
Some MCQs have placeholder references ('Unknown' title, page 1-2, rag_confidence 0.0) - requires verification of clinical accuracy without citation validation
agent_evaluations.additional_notes: Dataset contains 100 unique MCQs across depression, anxiety/bipolar, psychotic disorders, suicide risk/MHA, and mixed topics. Overall quality is good with strong adherence to Australian psychiatric guidelines (RANZCP, eTG, Mental Health Act). Main weaknesses: (1) SAFE-T framework not explicitly documented in explanations despite correct clinical management, (2) Cultural safety completely absent (no Aboriginal/TSI considerations), (3) Some repetition across template-generated MCQs (IDs 2000-2063 appear to be duplicates with similar scenarios). Recommend: Add SAFE-T checklist to depression/suicide MCQs, include cultural safety paragraph in all psychiatric MCQs, review duplicate MCQs for removal.
